title: Finite locally constant sheaves of sets are represented by finite etale schemes

source.place: Lemma Tag 03RV (lemma-characterize-finite-locally-constant), lines 9993-10023, with Definition Tag 03RU (definition-finite-locally-constant), lines 9915-9931; Lean: WeilConjectures.AlgebraicGeometry.HenselianFiniteEtale, AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.isFiniteLocallyConstant_yoneda_and_exists_iso, lines 91-111

proof.text: (Notation; restriction of a representable sheaf.) For an etale morphism $g:V\to Y$ and a presheaf $\mathcal G$ on $Y_{\Et}$, $\mathcal G|_V$ is the presheaf $W\mapsto\mathcal G(W)$ on $V_{\Et}$, an object $w:W\to V$ of $V_{\Et}$ being the object $g\circ w$ of $Y_{\Et}$ (etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] (2)); if $\mathcal G$ is a sheaf so is $\mathcal G|_V$, since a covering of $V_{\Et}$ is a covering of $Y_{\Et}$ with the same fibre products [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets]. For a $Y$-scheme $Q$ and an object $w:W\to V$ of $V_{\Et}$, the universal property of the fibre product $Q\times_YV$ [def-pc-fibre-product] gives the bijection $\operatorname{Mor}_Y(W,Q)\to\operatorname{Mor}_V(W,Q\times_YV)$, $a\mapsto(a,w)$, with inverse $b\mapsto\mathrm{pr}_1\circ b$; it commutes with composition by $V$-morphisms $W'\to W$. Hence $h_Q|_V\cong h_{Q\times_YV}$ as presheaves on $V_{\Et}$ (*), naturally in $Q$: for a $Y$-morphism $u:Q\to Q'$ it carries $h_u|_V$ to $h_{u\times_YV}$, and for a further etale $V'\to V$ the restriction of (*) to $V'$ composed with (*) for $Q\times_YV$ over $V'$ is (*) for $Q$ over $V'$, by the canonical isomorphism $(Q\times_YV)\times_VV'=Q\times_YV'$.

proof.text: (Part 1: $h_P$ is a sheaf.) Let $p:P\to Y$ be finite etale [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category]. By [lem-weil-pbc-small-etale-representable-presheaf-sheaf] (with $T=Y$, $X=P$) the presheaf $h_P$ is a sheaf of sets on $Y_{\Et}$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 03O3 (lemma-representable-sheaf-fpqc), used tacitly in Lemma Tag 03RV (lemma-characterize-finite-locally-constant), lines 9993-10023

proof.text:
(Part 1: $h_P$ is finite locally constant.) Let $y\in Y$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-etale-etale-local-split] there are an etale $g_y:U_y\to Y$, a point $u_y\in U_y$ with $g_y(u_y)=y$, a finite set $J_y$ and a decomposition $P\times_YU_y=\coprod_{j\in J_y}V_j$ into pairwise disjoint open and closed subschemes covering $P\times_YU_y$, each $\mathrm{pr}_2|_{V_j}:V_j\to U_y$ an isomorphism. Let $(U_y)_{J_y}=\coprod_{j\in J_y}U_y$ with coprojections $\iota_j$ and codiagonal $\pi$ [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family], and let $\theta:(U_y)_{J_y}\to P\times_YU_y$ be the morphism with $\theta\circ\iota_j=(\mathrm{pr}_2|_{V_j})^{-1}$ followed by the inclusion of $V_j$. Then $\mathrm{pr}_2\circ\theta=\pi$, and $\theta$ is an isomorphism: its restriction to the open subscheme $\iota_j(U_y)$ is an isomorphism onto the open subscheme $V_j$, these opens cover source and target and are pairwise disjoint on both sides, so the inverses glue to an inverse of $\theta$. The family $\{g_y:U_y\to Y\}_{y\in Y}$ consists of etale morphisms and is jointly surjective ($y=g_y(u_y)$), so it is a covering of $Y_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. For each $y$, by (*) of step 1, by $\theta$ (through $h_\theta$) and by [lem-galois-constant-sheaf-sets-representable] (with $U=U_y$, $E=J_y$) we get isomorphisms of sheaves on $(U_y)_{\Et}$
$$h_P|_{U_y}\cong h_{P\times_YU_y}\cong h_{(U_y)_{J_y}}\cong\underline{J_y},$$
with $J_y$ finite. With step 2, $h_P$ is a finite locally constant sheaf of sets on $Y_{\Et}$ in the sense of the statement. This proves (1).

source.place: Lemma Tag 03RV (lemma-characterize-finite-locally-constant), lines 9993-10023, proof, first two sentences ('A finite etale morphism is locally isomorphic to a disjoint union of isomorphisms, see Etale Morphisms, Lemma 04HN. Thus (2) implies (1).')

proof.text: (Part 2: local representing objects.) Let $\mathcal F$ be finite locally constant: a covering $\{g_i:Y_i\to Y\}_{i\in I}$ of $Y_{\Et}$, finite sets $S_i$ and isomorphisms $\mathcal F|_{Y_i}\cong\underline{S_i}$ on $(Y_i)_{\Et}$. Put $P_i=(Y_i)_{S_i}=\coprod_{s\in S_i}Y_i$ with codiagonal $\pi_i:P_i\to Y_i$ [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. By [lem-galois-constant-sheaf-sets-representable] (with $U=Y_i$, $E=S_i$) we obtain isomorphisms of sheaves $\beta_i:\mathcal F|_{Y_i}\xrightarrow{\sim}h_{P_i}$ on $(Y_i)_{\Et}$. Each $\pi_i$ is finite etale [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category]: etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-local-on-source], its restriction to each member $\iota_s(Y_i)$ of the open cover of $P_i$ being an isomorphism, hence an open immersion, hence etale [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] (1); finite by induction on $|S_i|$: for $S_i=\varnothing$, $P_i$ is empty and the preimage of every affine open of $Y_i$ is the empty affine scheme $\operatorname{Spec}0$, finite over it; for $|S_i|=1$, $\pi_i$ is an isomorphism, finite; and $(Y_i)_{S\sqcup\{s\}}=(Y_i)_S\amalg Y_i$ with $\pi_i$ induced by the two codiagonals, finite by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-coproduct] [lem-weil-pbc-finite-local-on-target].

source.place: Lemma Tag 03RV (lemma-characterize-finite-locally-constant), lines 9993-10023, proof: 'if F is finite locally constant, then there exists an etale covering {X_i -> X} such that F|_{X_i} is representable by U_i -> X_i finite etale'

proof.text:
(Part 2: the descent datum; the details the source omits.) For $i,j\in I$ put $Y_{ij}=Y_i\times_YY_j$ and for $i,j,k$ put $Y_{ijk}=Y_i\times_YY_j\times_YY_k$ [def-pc-fibre-product]; the projections $Y_{ij}\to Y_i$, $Y_{ij}\to Y_j$ are etale [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change], so $Y_{ij}$ is an object of $(Y_i)_{\Et}$, $(Y_j)_{\Et}$ and $Y_{\Et}$, and $(\mathcal F|_{Y_i})|_{Y_{ij}}=\mathcal F|_{Y_{ij}}=(\mathcal F|_{Y_j})|_{Y_{ij}}$ as presheaves (the composites $W\to Y_{ij}\to Y_i\to Y$ and $W\to Y_{ij}\to Y_j\to Y$ agree). Write $P_i|_{ij}=P_i\times_{Y_i}Y_{ij}$, an object of $(Y_{ij})_{\Et}$ ([lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change], $\pi_i$ etale by step 4). Let $\gamma_{ij}$ be the isomorphism of sheaves on $(Y_{ij})_{\Et}$
$$h_{P_i|_{ij}}\overset{(*)}{\cong}h_{P_i}|_{Y_{ij}}\xrightarrow{\beta_i^{-1}}\mathcal F|_{Y_{ij}}\xrightarrow{\beta_j}h_{P_j}|_{Y_{ij}}\overset{(*)}{\cong}h_{P_j|_{ij}}$$
((*) of step 1 applied over $Y_i$ and over $Y_j$). By [lem-galois-yoneda-fully-faithful] in the category $(Y_{ij})_{\Et}$ there is a unique $Y_{ij}$-morphism $\varphi_{ij}:P_i|_{ij}\to P_j|_{ij}$ with $h_{\varphi_{ij}}=\gamma_{ij}$, and it is an isomorphism (the morphism attached to $\gamma_{ij}^{-1}$ is its inverse, by the uniqueness in the same lemma). Cocycle: over $Y_{ijk}$ the pullbacks of $\varphi_{ij},\varphi_{jk},\varphi_{ik}$ correspond under (*) (with its compatibility under further restriction, step 1) to the restrictions of $\gamma_{ij},\gamma_{jk},\gamma_{ik}$ to $Y_{ijk}$, and $\gamma_{jk}\circ\gamma_{ij}=\gamma_{ik}$ there because the factors $\beta_j\beta_j^{-1}$ cancel; by the injectivity in [lem-galois-yoneda-fully-faithful] on $(Y_{ijk})_{\Et}$, $\varphi_{jk}\circ\varphi_{ij}=\varphi_{ik}$ over $Y_{ijk}$, and likewise $\varphi_{ii}=\mathrm{id}$. Now let $Y'=\coprod_iY_i$, $P'=\coprod_iP_i$ [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family] with the morphisms $Y'\to Y$ and $P'\to Y'$ induced by the $g_i$ and the $\pi_i$. $Y'\to Y$ is etale [lem-weil-pbc-etale-local-on-source] and surjective (the $g_i$ are jointly surjective); $P'\to Y'$ is finite etale, since over the open cover $\{Y_i\}$ of $Y'$ its restrictions are the $\pi_i$ [lem-weil-pbc-finite-local-on-target, lem-weil-pbc-etale-local-on-source]. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product], $Y''=Y'\times_YY'$ is covered by the pairwise disjoint open subschemes $Y_i\times_YY_j=Y_{ij}$, and $Y'''=Y'\times_YY'\times_YY'$ by the $Y_{ijk}$, and over $Y_{ij}$ the pullbacks $p_1^*P'$, $p_2^*P'$ are $P_i|_{ij}$, $P_j|_{ij}$. So the $\varphi_{ij}$ glue to an isomorphism $\varphi:p_1^*P'\to p_2^*P'$ over $Y''$, and the cocycle identities over the $Y_{ijk}$ give $p_{13}^*\varphi=p_{23}^*\varphi\circ p_{12}^*\varphi$ over $Y'''$: $(P',\varphi)$ is a finite etale $Y'$-scheme with a descent datum.

proof.text: (Part 2: effectivity.) By [lem-galois-descent] (applied to the surjective etale $Y'=\coprod_iY_i\to Y$ of step 5; its equivalence is base change $P\mapsto(P\times_YY',\text{canonical datum})$) there are a finite etale $Y$-scheme $P$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category] and an isomorphism $\psi:P\times_YY'\to P'$ of $Y'$-schemes compatible with the descent data. Restricting to the open $Y_i\subseteq Y'$ gives isomorphisms of $Y_i$-schemes $\psi_i:P\times_YY_i\to P_i$, and the compatibility says, over each $Y_{ij}$, that $\varphi_{ij}\circ(\psi_i\times_{Y_i}Y_{ij})=\psi_j\times_{Y_j}Y_{ij}$ as morphisms $P\times_YY_{ij}\to P_j|_{ij}$, where $(P\times_YY_i)\times_{Y_i}Y_{ij}=P\times_YY_{ij}=(P\times_YY_j)\times_{Y_j}Y_{ij}$ canonically [def-pc-fibre-product].

proof.text: (Part 2: $\mathcal F\cong h_P$.) For each $i$ let $\alpha_i:\mathcal F|_{Y_i}\to h_P|_{Y_i}$ be the isomorphism of sheaves on $(Y_i)_{\Et}$ given by $\beta_i$, then $h_{\psi_i^{-1}}:h_{P_i}\to h_{P\times_YY_i}$, then the inverse of (*) of step 1. By the definition of $\gamma_{ij}=h_{\varphi_{ij}}$ (step 5), the identity $\varphi_{ij}\circ(\psi_i\times_{Y_i}Y_{ij})=\psi_j\times_{Y_j}Y_{ij}$ (step 6) and the compatibility of (*) with restriction (step 1), $\alpha_i$ and $\alpha_j$ have the same restriction $\mathcal F|_{Y_{ij}}\to h_P|_{Y_{ij}}$. Let $w:W\to Y$ be an object of $Y_{\Et}$ and $s\in\mathcal F(W)$. Put $W_i=W\times_YY_i$, an object of $(Y_i)_{\Et}$ through its second projection; $\{W_i\to W\}_i$ is a covering of $Y_{\Et}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-base-change], and $W_i\times_WW_j=W\times_YY_{ij}$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Put $t_i=\alpha_i(s|_{W_i})\in h_P(W_i)$. By naturality of $\alpha_i,\alpha_j$ and their agreement on $Y_{ij}$, $t_i$ and $t_j$ have the same restriction to $W\times_YY_{ij}$. Since $h_P$ is a sheaf (step 2) [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets], there is a unique $t\in h_P(W)$ with $t|_{W_i}=t_i$ for all $i$; set $\alpha_W(s)=t$. Uniqueness of gluing shows that $\alpha_W$ is natural in $W$, i.e. $\alpha:\mathcal F\to h_P$ is a morphism of sheaves with $\alpha|_{Y_i}=\alpha_i$. The same construction with the $\alpha_i^{-1}$ (which also agree on the $Y_{ij}$), using that $\mathcal F$ is a sheaf, gives $\alpha':h_P\to\mathcal F$, and $\alpha'\alpha$, $\alpha\alpha'$ are the identities because their restrictions to every $W_i$ are, by uniqueness in the sheaf condition. So $\mathcal F\cong h_P$ with $P\to Y$ finite etale. This proves (2).

split_report.summary: Split along Stacks 03RV, whose proof was read with every lemma it cites (04HN, 02W5 and Remark 02W6, 0245, 02LA, 02VN; tags verified in tags/tags). The slopmaster2 declaration AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.isFiniteLocallyConstant_yoneda_and_exists_iso (HenselianFiniteEtale.lean 91-111) is a bare sorry with no decomposition, so the split follows the source; its notion IsFiniteLocallyConstantSheafOfTypes asks finite stalks instead of finite constant values (equivalent, not a mismatch for the node). Steps: (1) restriction to an etale V and h_Q|_V = h_{Q x_Y V} (universal property of fibre product); (2) h_P is a sheaf (lem-weil-pbc-small-etale-representable-presheaf-sheaf); (3) h_P finite locally constant via 04HN (lem-weil-pbc-finite-etale-etale-local-split) and the new node lem-galois-constant-sheaf-sets-representable (constant sheaf of sets E = h of the disjoint union of E copies, Stacks 03P5); (4) F|_{Y_i} = h_{P_i} with P_i = finite disjoint union of copies of Y_i, finite etale; (5) the descent datum, written out where 03RV says 'details omitted' (Yoneda on (Y_ij)_et gives phi_ij and the cocycle); (6) effectivity and finite-etaleness by lem-galois-descent (the unit's own finite etale descent node, which packages 0245 + 02LA + 02VN); (7) gluing of the local isomorphisms to F = h_P by the sheaf condition. New node: lem-galois-constant-sheaf-sets-representable (unsplit). Generic tools of unit sk-thm-p1 used as black boxes: lem-weil-pbc-finite-etale-etale-local-split (04HN) and lem-weil-pbc-small-etale-representable-presheaf-sheaf (03O3); the other cross-unit citations are Mathlib leaves.
